title: Morphometric analysis using multivariate statistical approaches for the prioritization of potential watersheds in Kuwait
content:
Abstract

Kuwait is a water-depleted country that is dry in summer and has temporary water accumulations during heavy precipitation in winter. The present study aims to determine the geomorphological characteristics of the drainage system which is useful in assessing the flow direction and accumulation location of surface water. The digital elevation model of the study area is processed to identify the spatial distribution of watersheds and their drainage system. Kuwait watershed morphometry analysis is a process to discriminate the morphometric parameters using multivariate statistical analyses and prioritized watersheds to rank the water potential watersheds. Twenty-nine geomorphological parameters were processed in principal component analysis and the strongly correlated parameters of principal component1, principal component2, and principal component3 were interpreted as geometric, soil erosion, and relief aspects, respectively. As a result, watershed2, watershed7, watershed6, and watershed5 in principal component1; watershed11, watershed9, watershed8, and watershed10 in principal component2; and watershed9, watershed4, watershed6, and watershed11 in principal component3 are high-ranked watersheds with respective group. To verify these three classes, the rotated principal component analysis weighted sum compound parameter was processed by the highly correlated principal component’s first six parameters which revealed that watershed4, watershed8, watershed9, and watershed10 are high-ranked watersheds. The combination of these four classes of processes revealed that watershed4, watershed9, and watershed11 are high-ranked watersheds possessing more runoff possibility during the rainy season. Watershed9, watershed10, and watershed11 are having high relief and short mainstreams, hence could be a source of flooding during heavy storms.
